title: Structured memory versus a recent-event window on synthetic key recall
question: With equal record capacity, does keyed memory improve latest-value recall in noisy event streams?
hypothesis: Storing the latest value of each key may improve recall relative to retaining recent events.
limitations: This is a synthetic engineering demonstration, not a novel research contribution or a competition-ready paper.
No language model or autonomous scientific agent is used in the offline experiment.
Capacity is measured in records, not tokens or bytes; equal record counts do not imply equal memory cost.
The generated distribution favors retrieval of structured key-value facts; conclusions do not establish general agent capability.
Seeds repeat one task generator; they are not independent real-world benchmarks.
